title: Phoenix Protocol: Verify S3 visibility using account-level listing (read-only, deterministic).
objectives: Identify the AWS CLI command for listing S3 buckets
Understand the concept of bucket visibility at the account level
Determine the correct IAM permissions required for S3 listing

mission_brief.situation: You are operating as a secure cloud operator in an authorized sandbox where resources may or may not exist.
mission_brief.mission: Verify access safely using read-only AWS CLI commands without assuming any pre-existing resources.
mission_brief.execution: Run discovery-only commands and validate success by deterministic behavior (successful execution), not resource presence.

content.concept: When attempting to list all S3 buckets in an account, it is essential to understand that some buckets may be hidden due to various reasons such as incorrect permissions or misconfigured settings. To verify S3 visibility at the account level, one must use the 'aws s3 ls' command with the correct IAM permissions.
content.walkthrough: To start, ensure you have the AWS CLI configured with the necessary credentials and permissions. Then, run the following command: aws s3 ls --recursive --output json. This will list all S3 buckets in the account, including any that may be hidden due to incorrect permissions or misconfigured settings.
checkpoints: Verify that IAM permissions are set up correctly for S3 listing
Check if bucket policies are restricting access to certain buckets
Ensure that S3 versioning is enabled and configured properly
common_mistakes: Assuming all S3 buckets are visible by default
Not checking IAM permissions for S3 listing
Misconfiguring bucket policies or S3 settings

lab.setup: Ensure AWS CLI is configured with sandbox credentials. Do not create, modify, or delete any resources.
safety: Use read-only AWS CLI commands only (list/describe/get).
Do not reference named resources unless the lesson explicitly created them (this v2 track does not).
If you see AccessDenied, stop and verify permissions rather than trying write actions.

elite_competence.role_simulation: A security engineer must verify S3 visibility at the account level using the 'aws s3 ls' command with correct IAM permissions.

bug_injection.bug: Operator assumes resources must exist and mislabels empty output as failure.
bug_injection.symptom: Student reports 'nothing returned' and believes permissions are broken.
bug_injection.fix: Explain empty-sandbox behavior and validate by successful execution + no errors, not by finding assets.

pass_conditions: The output of the 'aws s3 ls --recursive --output json' command contains a list of all S3 buckets in the account
IAM permissions are set up correctly for S3 listing
Bucket policies are not restricting access to certain buckets
fail_conditions: The output of the 'aws s3 ls --recursive --output json' command does not contain a list of all S3 buckets in the account
IAM permissions are not set up correctly for S3 listing

interrogation_questions: What IAM permission is required to list all S3 buckets in an account?
How can bucket policies restrict access to certain buckets?
What should be checked if the 'aws s3 ls --recursive --output json' command does not return expected results?

legal_context.allowed: Executing read-only AWS CLI commands in an authorized sandbox or training account.
legal_context.prohibited: Creating, deleting, or modifying AWS resources without explicit authorization.

resume_bullets: Verified S3 visibility at the account level using the 'aws s3 ls' command with correct IAM permissions
Ensured that IAM permissions are set up correctly for S3 listing
Checked bucket policies and S3 settings to prevent access restrictions
